summary: Implement the already-planned notification center with a tenant-scoped canonical inbox, recipient preferences, dedupe/severity semantics, immutable delivery evidence and first Web UI plus durable-webhook provider adapters.

impacts.evidence: Inbox, preferences and delivery evidence are keyed by organization/workspace; API scope and recipient identity come only from the authenticated resolver, and PostgreSQL repeats tenant predicates under forced RLS.

Notifications contain bounded presentation text and optional canonical entity/source references. Delivery history stores no provider body, header, credential or raw error; obvious credential-shaped notification text is rejected before persistence/fan-out; external webhook delivery is explicit opt-in.
Additive notification inbox, read-state, delivery-history and preference endpoints are documented in OpenAPI 0.6.0 with strict Draft 2020-12 schemas.
The webhook adapter emits one new versioned event type platform.notifications.notification_created.v1 with a catalogued bounded payload schema; it does not mutate existing event contracts.
Connector SDK interfaces and provider admission remain unchanged. Notification providers are an internal platform port, not connector plugins.
Expand migration 000021 adds notification inbox, preferences and immutable channel delivery evidence only; no existing column/table is contracted.
Authenticated recipient binding prevents cross-user inbox selection. Webhook provider delegates signing, HTTPS/DNS policy, retry and DLQ to Task 063 rather than duplicating egress logic.
Task 022 communicates facts and does not authorize or perform privileged commerce mutations. Approval policy remains owned by Task 017.

Immutable per-occurrence/per-attempt channel evidence records status, bounded machine error code and attempt time without raw provider responses or credentials. Notification read state is mutable presentation state and does not replace Task 003 audit or Task 030 lineage.

Unique tenant/workspace/recipient/dedupe keys collapse repeated conditions under a serialized advisory lock. Distinct occurrences increment deterministically without fan-out, monotonic severity escalation is re-delivered, and the same source occurrence can be replayed after transient provider failure without incrementing the business occurrence count.
Notification webhook delivery is an adapter over Task 063's durable webhook handler. No direct HTTP client, DNS resolver, signing key or retry implementation is introduced in notifications.
Inbox timestamps, occurrence counts and immutable delivery status/error-code evidence support later notification SLO metrics; production alert thresholds remain Task 066.
Migration 000021 is additive and older binaries can ignore the new tables. Disabling notification producers/providers stops new writes without destructive schema rollback.

Tests cover dedupe, concurrent serialization boundary, occurrence counting, same-occurrence provider replay with append-only attempts, monotonic escalation, safe preference defaults, provider failure/unavailability classification, immutable retry attempts, credential-shaped text rejection, durable-webhook delegation, authenticated recipient binding, strict API JSON, schema pair/error invariants and migration RLS/immutability controls.
